content.text: {"vat": "Worker's flat cap (peaked cap), worn by a bricklayer on a scaffold", "dac_diem": "Dark, rounded, soft cap with a short stiff brim at the front and a fitted crown. The man wears it with a short-sleeved pale collarless shirt and a dark waistcoat. Around him are a brick chimney, roof timbers and a scaffold lashed with rope.", "co_tu_nam": 1890, "da_co_nam_1667": "no", "ly_do": "Wool caps existed in the 1600s, but this look is a later one: a tailored, brimmed flat or baker-boy cap, worn with a modern work shirt and waistcoat. It is typical of the late 19th to early 20th century, not of 1667 London."}
